newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly up on Wednesday on overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at 23,400 yuan ($2,821) per tonne, rising 120 yuan. It opened at an intraday high of 23,500 and hit a low of 23,320.
June fell 20 to 22,650, July rose 20 to 22,900, August 110 to 23,160, October 120 to 23,520 and November 100 to 23,500.
Combined volume rose to 33,120 tonnes from 29,310.
Copper opened higher and liquidation by long-positions holders pushed the prices down for most of the session but the contracts still ended higher than Tuesday's close.
Traders said the LME gains boosted confidence of long-position holders but prices met strong resistance at high levels.

"The LME gains triggered short-covering but many investors were willing to liquidate their long positions at high levels," one trader said. "Copper met strong resistance mainly because many investors believed it would fall shortly due to poor market fundamentals."
Traders said domestic demand was weak despite weakening physical prices in the recent weeks. Physical prices are around 22,900 yuan in the Shanghai area.
"Physical prices have fallen nearly 600 yuan over the past few weeks but still few investors want to buy at the current level," a second trader said.
Traders said they expected copper to fall in the next few days.
Aluminium ended mixed. June rose 80 to 14,580, July was unchanged at 14,700, August rose 50 to 15,050, September fell 50 to 14,950 and October shed 370 to 14,950.
Combined volume rose to 2,820 tonnes from 1,180.
